messages.author: 48e6e7f4ac40bb80
messages.subject: using the dredge function with gdistsamp
parts:
When trying to use the dredge function I am encountering an error that I have been unable to find any documentation on here or elsewhere:

Error in umf_get_specs(x) : unknown "unmarkedFitGDS" model structure

Below is the code for my unmarked frame, global model, and dredge function. 

APPA15umf<-unmarkedFrameGDS(y=as.matrix(data[,2:7]),
                         siteCovs=(fin.covs),
                         numPrimary=1, 
                         yearlySiteCovs = data.frame(fin.detcovs),
                         dist.breaks=c(0,20,40,60,80,100,120),
                         unitsIn="m", survey="point")

glob.mod<-gdistsamp(~SiteAge+Acres+elev+prism15+sap15+shrb15+forb15+grass15+bare15+RGsm15+RGmd15+RGlg15,~1,~1, data=APPA15umf, output="density", mixture="P")

df<-dredge(glob.mod, beta="none",evaluate="TRUE",rank="AICc",m.lim=c(NA,10))

I have also tried the dredge funciton, eliminating the beta, evaluate, rank, and m.lim arguments with the same result. Any insight as to what might be generating this error would be much appreciated. Additionally, if there is another function that folks might recommend in lieu of the dredge function, please share! 

Thank you!

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: using the dredge function with gdistsamp
parts:
I don't think there is an easy answer short of changes to package MuMIn to explicitly support these model types.

A while back I wrote an unmarked-specific version of dredge that should work with nearly all the unmarked functions, but without as many features as MuMIn::dredge (e.g. , forcing some terms to be in all models).

https://github.com/kenkellner/unmarked/blob/fitModels/R/fitModels.R

You could install this with a specific dev version of unmarked:

devtools::install_github("kenkellner/unmarked", ref="fitModels")

And try it with something like the code below:

library(unmarked)
?fitModels
?dredge

#Simulate pcountOpen data
set.seed(3)
M <- 50
T <- 5
lambda <- 4
gamma <- 1.5
omega <- 0.8
p <- 0.7
y <- N <- matrix(NA, M, T)
S <- G <- matrix(NA, M, T-1)
N[,1] <- rpois(M, lambda)
for(t in 1:(T-1)) {
    S[,t] <- rbinom(M, N[,t], omega)
    G[,t] <- rpois(M, gamma)
    N[,t+1] <- S[,t] + G[,t]
}
y[] <- rbinom(M*T, N, p)
     
# Prepare data
sc <- as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(50*2),ncol=2))
names(sc) <- c('sc1','sc2')
umf <- unmarkedFramePCO(y = y, siteCovs=sc, numPrimary=T)

# Fit model
m1 <- pcountOpen(~sc1+sc2, ~1, ~1, ~1, ,mixture = "ZIP", umf, K=20)

#Fit all subsets in parallel
dr <- unmarked::dredge(m1, parallel=TRUE)

#Get AIC table
modSel(dr)

Given the disagreement over whether 'dredging' is a good approach to model selection in general I don't know if this functionality will end up in the release version of unmarked.

Ken
